objective: For each route of the frozen transfer statement (bit PHP and its relatives by a parity-preserving reduction; Braun's generic criterion; lifting theorems with stifling gadgets; the count's own xor-lift), prove the step at which it fails for the sphere's count, or give the transfer.
status: Obstructed 2026-11-10 (proved): no route of the frozen transfer statement carries a regular, depth-restricted or dag-like Res(xor) bound to the sphere's count. Braun's criterion is capped at exp(d^2/(6v)) by the count's polynomial-calculus degree O(sqrt n); bit PHP would need a parity reduction from PIGEON to the count (none by ordinary decision trees, PPP^dt not in PPADS^dt); stifling gadgets are never affine; the xor-lift is the count again.
title: Where each Res(xor) route to the count stops
